candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — medication-error prevention and safe administration processes
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — time-critical medication safety
candidate.educational_objective: Follow medication-specific and organization-approved timing requirements for time-critical scheduled medications.

options.A: Administer it within the medication-specific, organization-defined timing window.
options.B: Administer it at any convenient time during the shift.
options.C: Use the same broad timing window used for all non-time-critical medications.
options.D: Delay it whenever unit workflow becomes busy, regardless of the medication's timing requirements.

candidate.rationale: ISMP distinguishes time-critical scheduled medications from medications for which a broader administration window is acceptable. A time-critical medication should be administered according to the organization-approved, medication-specific timing window because clinically important early or delayed dosing may cause harm or reduce therapeutic effect. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Time-critical scheduled medications require medication-specific timely administration rather than a universal broad administration window.
candidate.source_document_title: ISMP Acute Care Guidelines for Timely Administration of Scheduled Medications
candidate.source_locator: Guideline rationale distinguishing time-sensitive medications from a one-size-fits-all scheduled-medication timing rule
candidate.source_version_date: 2011 guideline; current ISMP/ECRI resource page checked 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: A medication is designated by the hospital as time-critical. Which nursing action is most appropriate?
